title: Beginner Python Mistake Case
description: Schema for one benchmark case used by the SIT724 feedback-evaluation pipeline. Q1-Q10 are the SIT723 baseline cases (status: final, verbatim from the SIT723 thesis). Q11+ are SIT724 Sprint 1 expansion cases (status: draft until reviewed by the supervisor).

id.description: Unique case identifier, e.g. Q1, Q11.

topic.description: Lower-kebab-case topic tag used for coverage reporting, e.g. 'integer-division'.

status.description: 'final' cases are locked and enter evaluation runs. 'draft' cases are excluded from runs until promoted to 'final' by the validator config or a supervisor sign-off note in decision_log.md.

difficulty.description: Difficulty tier from the SIT724 Benchmark Difficulty Tiers doc (v1.0, 8 Sep 2026), classified case-by-case on two dimensions from novice-programmer research (Qian & Lehman 2017; du Boulay's notional machine): error visibility (SyntaxError / runtime exception / silent wrong output) and depth of misconception (single surface fact vs notional-machine model of execution). easy = visible failure or single fact, one-step reasoning. medium = runtime exception, or silent but a single well-known rule. hard = silent failure and/or multi-step state tracing and/or notional-machine misconception. Tier sizes fall out of the classification (10/12/8), not a forced even split. Added per supervisor feedback (19 Aug 2026).

question.description: The code snippet or question shown to the student.

wrong_answer.description: The common wrong answer a beginner gives.

misconception.description: One-sentence label for the underlying misconception.

notes.description: Optional free-text notes (e.g. supervisor review status).
